rv.q: Alan Strachan ’s cleverly orchestrated revival of his second big hit, first seen in Scarborough in 1969, reminds us just what a comic master Ayckbourn is.
Alan Strachan's production, staunchly true to the original Sixties setting, is efficient rather than inspired and could do with more pace.
This is a triumphant return of an outstanding farce: vintage Ayckbourn, classic production.

cn.t: Critics praise this revival of Ayckbourn's vintage comedy as hilarious and technically ingenious, with sharp writing that remains surprisingly relevant. The production earns acclaim for its comic mastery and poignant observations on class and relationships.
